units.name: Days top
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI), pointer and keyboard, reviewed with the desktop rules at 900x560 (compact height), 1360x860 and 1728x1084, dark and light at 1360. Evidence is days.rs lines 1-1138, the slot, host and usage row code in days-lower.rs, theme.rs, kit.rs and five screenshots; nothing was driven with real input, because this is a native app and not a browser page. First impression: the page reads as organised, with a clear header, an even tile row and consistent cards. No blurred audit was run, but by eye the saturated week chart takes the attention, while the timeline, which is the day itself, is pale and mostly empty. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 4 Major, 11 Minor, 3 Cosmetic. The top problem is that nothing on the page can be reached from the keyboard. Close behind, the timeline's state colours have no key, its fills are almost invisible when unlabelled, and the first KPI row shows numbers that don't add up.

units.name: Days lower cards
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI), pointer and keyboard, lower Days page. Evidence is the code slice, the full days.rs and theme.rs, and 5 captures. Nothing was driven with real input, because this is a native window and the browser can't open it. Contrast is computed from theme hex values. Sizes seen: about 1363 CSS px wide (days-tall.png, days-900.png, days-dark.png) and 900 wide (days-s.png). First impression: the left column reads as organised, with the week, the timeline, then task lists. The right rail is a stack of same-looking cards that switch between day and week without saying so, and at 900 wide it falls under everything in a half-width column with the other half empty. Counts: 0 catastrophe, 4 major, 12 minor, 1 cosmetic. Top problem: the lower cards don't reliably say which period they describe. "This week" is hard-coded even when an earlier week is shown, and "Agent time by project" is one day's figure sitting under a week chart with almost the same name, so "webapp 100%" reads as false on a page that exists to show how the work went.

units.name: Weekly review
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI), pointer and keyboard, reviewed from code plus 8 captures at 900x560, 1360x860, 1568x1250 and 1728x1084, in dark and light. Nothing was driven with real input, because this is a native app and the browser driver can't reach it. First impression: the page reads as organised. Judged by eye (the blur audit wasn't run), the week, four KPIs, one primary button and the stacked bar come through in the right order, and the chrome stays quiet. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 2 Major, 11 Minor, 3 Cosmetic. The top problem is that the page answers only half of "how the work went and what shipped". It reports time and nothing about output, and it colours less agent time green, so a week where nothing finished looks like a good one. The other Major is that no control on the page can be reached from the keyboard.

units.name: Releases overview
units.verdict: Reviewed the macOS desktop Releases overview (GPUI, pointer and keyboard) at 900x560, 1360x860 and 1728x1084, in dark at all three sizes and light at 1360x860. Evidence is four captures plus releases.rs and the app.rs, kit.rs and theme.rs code around it. The native app could not be driven, so behaviour comes from reading the code. First impression: the page reads as organised and calm. Version numbers and the blue Unreleased tile lead the eye, and chrome stays quiet, but the two cards fill only part of the space at the larger sizes. Counts: 0 catastrophe, 3 major, 8 minor, 1 cosmetic. The top problem is that the overview does not answer one of its primary questions: "v0.14.0 pending" gives no progress, and a cut that can no longer finish looks the same as a healthy one. The other majors are that no control on the page can be reached by keyboard, and that a failed project fetch shows "Loading…" forever. Data-related findings note where the sample may be the cause.

units.name: Project releases
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI), reviewed at 900x560, 1360x860, 1568x1250 and 1728x1084. Dark at all sizes; light at 1360x860 and 1568x1250. The evidence is 10 captures plus releases.rs and the code it calls, so nothing was used with real input: the app can't run in the browser driver, which I used only for contrast maths. First impression: the page reads as organised. The orange Next cut band draws the eye first, then v0.13.0, and the monthly rows are calm and easy to scan. The weakness is inside Unreleased, where the checklist and the work list overlap without saying how they relate, and everything older sits about 1000px down even with sample data. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 3 Major, 6 Minor, 4 Cosmetic. Top problem: the page doesn't clearly answer "what is in v0.14.0, and what is it still waiting for?". Three lists and three kinds of count overlap, and a cut that can no longer happen still reads as an ordinary "1 of 5 ready" (R15).

units.name: Flow 6 Review to fixes
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI), pointer and keyboard. I reviewed captures at 1360x860 and 1568x1250, plus the code; the live app was not run, so nothing was measured or driven with real input. The Weekly review row and the real pre-checked landing are unseen and judged from code. First impression: the Review page reads as organised. The week and four numbers come first, then Suggested fixes with the only filled button, and the time breakdowns sit quieter below. The handover is the weak part. Findings: 0 Catastrophe, 3 Major, 6 Minor, 1 Cosmetic. Top problem: the person can't tell what Plan a goal will do. The label promises a goal, the card says 3, and only a hover tooltip says 2 fixes get checked on another page. Backlog then gives no sign that the checks came from the review, and no on-screen way back.

units.name: Flow 8 Release view
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (GPUI), pointer and keyboard, dark theme. I reviewed 7 captures at 1728x1084, 1360x860 and 900x560, plus the code for the Releases pages, the sidebar and the app shell. The evidence is code and screenshots only: this is a native app, so nothing was driven with real input. First impression: the project page reads as organised, with a clear order of Next cut, Unreleased, newest release, then months. It is heavy, though, with boxes three deep and an alarm-coloured bar for a normal waiting state. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 4 Major, 12 Minor, 2 Cosmetic. The top problem is that the flow is pointer-only: release rows, task links, goal links and PR links can't be reached from the keyboard, and the reason a cut can't finish is in a hover tooltip. The next most costly problem is that the task panel covers the state, PR and date columns at 1360 and leaves 172px of the page at 900, so the owner can't watch the Next cut list while reading a task.

findings.title: No Days control can be reached from the keyboard
findings.element: Days › header (project toggles, ‹ › Today, Day/Week), week card (columns, day tiles), timeline (bars, marks), at every size and theme
findings.problem: None of these controls has tab_index or track_focus, and no key is bound for stepping dates; the only Days binding is Cmd-6 to open the page. A keyboard user can open the page but can't change the day, filter a project, open a task from a bar or read any tooltip. There is no focus indicator because nothing takes focus.
findings.principle: Every function works from the keyboard, with a visible focus indicator; arrows move inside groups [WCAG 2.1.1] [WCAG 2.4.7] [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give toggles, ‹ ›, Today, Day/Week, day tiles and bars a tab stop with a 2px t.accent focus ring, and make Enter or Space activate them. Treat the day tiles as one group with Left and Right arrows. Bind Left and Right to earlier and later day and T to Today when no text field has focus (Cmd-Left and Cmd-Right are already NavBack and NavForward). Show the tooltip on focus as well as on hover.

findings.title: Timeline bar states are colour-only and have no key
findings.element: Days › timeline card › bars and legend, all sizes, both themes (days-dark-m.png, days-light-m.png)
findings.problem: The legend covers only the five marks. Green, blue, orange, red and grey bars are never explained, so reading T1 as done or the second T3 bar as waiting on you means hovering each bar. Colour is the only resting signal, and pairs share a colour: failed and lost are both red, stopped and away are both grey.
findings.principle: Colour isn't the only signal [WCAG 1.4.1]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Add a bar key to the legend row as a separate group: Working, Done, Waiting on you, Failed or lost, Stopped or away. Add a non-colour cue on bars: a diagonal hatch on waiting, a left 2px edge on failed or lost, and a dashed outline on stopped or away. This keeps the tooltip's wording for the exact state.

findings.title: Timeline fills nearly vanish against the card
findings.element: Days › timeline card › unlabelled bars, Running bars, slot-pool bands; both themes, clearest on the sliver after T1 in days-light-m.png
findings.problem: Bars have soft fills and no border, so their edge against the card is about 1.1-1.2:1: accent_soft is 1.16:1 in light and 1.17:1 in dark, seg 1.19:1 and 1.13:1, up_soft about 1.14:1. Labelled bars survive on their text. The code comment says most bars are too narrow for a label, so most of a real day is a barely visible clickable shape. Non-peak Running bars are 1.32:1 in light and 1.49:1 in dark.
findings.principle: Graphics needed to understand the content, and control boundaries, reach 3:1 [WCAG 1.4.11]
findings.fix: Keep the soft fill for labelled bars and add a 1px border in each state's strong colour (t.accent, t.up, t.warn, t.down, t.faint), which all reach 3:1 or close to it on the card; check t.faint in light, at 3.04:1. Paint bars under the label width solid in that strong colour. Replace accent_line on Running with t.faint or a mid accent at 3:1, keeping t.accent for the peak. Use the same strong edge on slot-pool bands.

findings.title: KPI tiles show a saving their own numbers contradict
findings.element: Days › KPI tiles › Agent time and Human estimate; also the week's Hours saved line (days-dark-m.png)
findings.problem: The tiles read Agent time 5h 36m, Human estimate 6h, 4h saved, yet 6h minus 5h 36m is 24m. The saving uses est_agent_min while the tile beside it shows agent_min, and both are simply called agent time. The same gap shows on the week: the card says 24h agent while the chart's bars add up to about 27h. The owner can't tell which number to trust when judging how the work went. The values are sample data, but the two fields are in the code.
findings.principle: One fact, one place, and no copies that can disagree [SEC-7]; match the user's words [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Show the sum the saving really uses, for example delta text "4h saved vs 2h estimated agent time", or compute saved from the agent time on display. Apply the same name in the Hours saved breakdown: "79h human estimate − 24h estimated agent". If the two agent times stay separate, name them differently everywhere.

findings.title: "This week" stays on the cards when an earlier week is shown
findings.element: Days › rail › Hours saved this week and Tasks done this week (titles and legends), on any day outside the current week, all sizes
findings.problem: The daemon builds the week from the selected date (week_start(date, ...)), but saved_card and done_card hard-code "this week" and "last week". Go back to October and the card still says "Hours saved this week" over October's numbers. Going back to earlier days is a stated purpose of the page, so the owner can misread an old week as the current one. The left cards already use v.week_label correctly.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status and truthful readouts [NNG-H1]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Use the same pattern as the left column: h2(format!("Hours saved · {}", v.week_label)) and h2(format!("Tasks done · {}", v.week_label)). Keep "this week" only when the shown week contains today. Change the legends and the vs_last line to "shown week" / "week before" in the same case.

findings.title: The rail mixes day and week scopes and repeats the same facts
findings.element: Days › rail (Notable, Hours saved, Waiting on you, Tasks done, Agent time by project, Planning): days-tall.png, days-900.png, days-s.png
findings.problem: Six same-looking cards alternate scope: Notable (day), Hours saved (week), Waiting on you (day, unlabelled), Tasks done (week), Agent time by project (day, unlabelled), Planning (30 days). "Agent time by project" reads webapp 100% directly below a page whose "Agent time · Nov 1 – Nov 7" chart shows api and webapp, because it comes from day["by_project"]. Facts repeat: 36m is the KPI, the Notable lead, the Waiting on you total and its median; 5h 36m is both KPI and split total; each day's done count is on the week tiles and again in the Tasks done chart. Reading the rail means working out each card's period one at a time.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; group by function [SEC-1]; every element earns its place [SCR-5] [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: Reorder the rail by scope: Notable, Waiting on you, Agent time by project (the selected day), then Hours saved, Tasks done, Planning (longer spans). Put the day in the two unlabelled titles with the finished_card logic: "Waiting on you today" / "Waiting on you on Friday, November 6", and the same for "Agent time by project". Remove the 24px total from Waiting on you, since the KPI already holds it, and lead with the strip and "median 36m · usual 18m". Drop the "longest wait" Notable line when there is only one wait.

findings.title: Waiting time in the task bars is hard to see and has no number
findings.element: Days › How long tasks took › bar wait segment: T14 in days-tall.png, T23 in days-900.png; light and dark
findings.problem: The wait segment butts straight against the work segment with no gap, and the two are separated only by hue: warn against api blue is 1.17:1 light and 1.72:1 dark; warn against webapp amber is 2.39:1 light and 1.45:1 dark. Amber and orange are also close hues, although the palette comment says oranges are left out. The row prints only the total, so the wait in minutes exists only in a hover tooltip. This is the card's second meaning and the part the owner can act on.
findings.principle: Non-text contrast [WCAG 1.4.11]; use of colour [WCAG 1.4.1]
findings.fix: Add a 2px card-colour gap between the segments: left(relative(work)) plus ml(px(2.)). Give the wait segment a shape difference, such as a 2px top and bottom border or diagonal stripes. Print the wait in the row: "2h 48m" with a muted "32m wait" in the state column when no state is set. Replace the webapp amber slot with a hue further from warn, then re-run the palette's colour-blind check.

findings.title: Rows and chart details can't be reached from the keyboard
findings.element: Days › How long tasks took rows, Done today rows, Show all link, Waiting on you squares, Tasks done bars; all sizes
findings.problem: days.rs has no focus handle, tab stop or key handling. Task rows and Done rows open the right panel on click only, the Show all link is a clickable div, and every hover tooltip (work and wait split, PR state, each wait, each day's counts) is pointer-only. Without a mouse the owner can't open a task from this page or read those numbers. The rows also have no focus style. Search can still find a task, so it isn't a dead end, but this page's list can't be used.
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; focus visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; arrows move within groups [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give each list one focus handle via track_focus, as backlog.rs does: Up and Down move a selected row, Enter runs m.open_task, and the focused row gets a 2px accent outline. Make Show all a tab stop operated with Enter or Space. Show a focused row's tooltip content while it has focus, or print it in the row (see R7).

findings.title: No control on the page can be reached by keyboard
findings.element: Weekly review › all controls (‹, All weeks and its menu, ›, Day/Week, Plan a goal, fix rows, task rows, Commands tabs), all sizes and themes
findings.problem: Every control is a clickable div with no tab stop, focus state or key handler, so week navigation and acting on fixes need a mouse. The only keys that work here are global ones such as Cmd+R, Cmd+Left and Esc. A search of taskboard-app/src found no tab_index, tab_stop or focus-style calls, and track_focus appears only on MainWindow and Settings. The cause is in the shared kit, so this is likely app-wide.
findings.principle: Keyboard operable, focus visible, arrows within groups [WCAG 2.1.1] [WCAG 2.4.7] [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give kit::btn, kit::seg items, kit::menu_item and clickable rows a tab index and Enter/Space activation, with a 2px accent focus ring at 3:1 or better. Make each seg and the week menu one tab stop with arrow keys inside, opening the menu on the selected week. Add `[` and `]` for earlier and later week, shown in the ‹ › tooltips.

findings.title: The week shows time spent but nothing about what got done
findings.element: Weekly review › KPIs and deltas (review-dark-m.png, review-light-m.png)
findings.problem: The owner opens this page to see how the work went and what shipped, but all four KPIs and every card measure time or failures. The review data has no tasks finished, goals completed or releases. Delta code treats less as better for every number, so Agent time '↓ 1.0 h less' is green even if output fell. An idle week would look like the best week, which is a wrong reading on the page's main job.
findings.principle: Walkthrough question 4, progress toward the goal [NNG-CW]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; match to the real world [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Add a read-only 'Shipped' KPI and card first: tasks finished, goals completed and releases in the period, each with its change. Tasks open in the right panel, goals go to their page, and releases link to the Releases page. This needs new fields in the review data. Make the Agent time delta neutral (t.muted, arrow kept) and keep green and red for Waiting on you, Timeouts and Failed, then rerun.

findings.title: The card hides how far the next cut has got, and whether it is dead
findings.element: Releases › project card › Unreleased tile › pending pill, all sizes and themes (webapp in releases-dark-m.png, releases-light-m.png)
findings.problem: The pill says only "v0.14.0 pending". To learn what the cut waits for, the owner must open each project page. A cut with a Dead item ("the cut will be dropped") looks the same as a healthy one, so the one state that needs attention is invisible on the overview. While cutting, the pill also keeps the warn tone (line 774), although the project page uses the working tone for the same state (line 454).
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; frequent in view, rare behind [SEC-8]
findings.fix: Build the pill from the existing Pending::progress(): "v0.14.0 · 1 of 3 ready", or "v0.14.0 · Cutting" in the working tone. If any item is Standing::Dead, use the failed tone and "v0.14.0 · Can't finish". Make the header summary count these too, for example "1 pending cut · 1 can't finish". This is display only and adds no actions.

findings.title: Nothing on the overview works from the keyboard
findings.element: Releases › every card control ("N releases" link, latest block, Unreleased tile, previous release rows), all sizes
findings.problem: Every control is a div with on_click, with no focus handle. A search of crates/taskboard-app/src finds no tab_index or tab stop at all, so this limit is probably app-wide. Unlike Board, Projects, Goals, Backlog and Days, Releases also has no Cmd-number shortcut. A keyboard user cannot reach the page's controls, open a release or see focus. This is an all-day tool for a developer on a Mac.
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; focus visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; arrows move inside groups [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give each card target a tab stop with a 2px accent focus ring, with Enter opening it. Inside a card, make the rows one stop that Up and Down arrows move through. Add a GoReleases action on Cmd-4, which is unbound today, and list it in the View menu. The same pattern is needed across the app, so the kit is the place to add it.

findings.title: A failed project fetch shows "Loading…" forever
findings.element: Releases › project card › loading state, from code (overview_card lines 736-738; app.rs lines 1462-1466)
findings.problem: A failed GET /releases is dropped by `if let Ok(v)`, so the list stays None and the card reads "Loading…" with no end and no error. The header summary also stays hidden. If the board is down, the banner explains it, but the card still claims to be loading. If only that project's call fails, nothing on screen says anything is wrong.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; help users recognize and recover from errors [NNG-H9]
findings.fix: Keep the last error per project in releases::State. In the card, show "Can't load api's releases." with a Try again link that calls refresh. Refreshing is not an edit, so it fits the read-only rule. When m.down is set, show "Can't load the board." instead of "Loading…".

findings.title: Unreleased doesn't say how the Next cut relates to the work listed under it
findings.element: Project page › Unreleased section, all sizes (rel-webapp-dark-m.png, rel-webapp-light-m.png, rel-webapp-dark-s.png)
findings.problem: The section holds two overlapping lists with no stated link. The heading says '3 tasks · 1 goal' and the pill says '1 of 3 ready', but those 3s count different things. G4 appears twice, as '2 of 3' in the checklist and '2 tasks' in the card just below. T1 and T68 are in the checklist but in no list under it, which may be the sample's data. The owner can't tell whether T65 to T67 ship in v0.14.0 or whether the checklist is the whole cut. Three levels of nested boxes (section, checklist, goal cards) make it harder to see which list is the main one.
findings.principle: Failed checks: one fact, one place [SEC-7]; grouped by space, containers only where space can't do it [SEC-2]; consistent naming [NNG-H4]; progress the user can read [NNG-H1]. A primary surface, so 3 Major.
findings.fix: Display only, nothing here edits a cut. (1) Reword the pill to say what remains: '2 still to finish' instead of '1 of 3 ready'. (2) Add one line under the Next cut header stating the rule, for example 'Cuts when these finish, with the work below'. Confirm the wording against how `tb` builds a cut, which I couldn't see. (3) Use one count form for a goal in both places: 'G4 2 of 3 done' in the card header too. (4) Label the lower group, for example 'Finished so far', so it isn't read as more checklist. (5) Remove the outer section box around Unreleased, keeping the heading on the page, so only the checklist and goal cards are boxed.

findings.title: A cut that can't happen still reads as ordinary progress
findings.element: Project page › Next cut header and checklist rows › Standing::Dead (next_cut, Pending::progress); not in the sample, so not captured
findings.problem: The code says a dead item means the cut will be dropped, yet the header keeps its warn band and the pill keeps counting: the test asserts '1 of 5 ready' with a dead item present. The owner could wait on a release that will never come. The only reason is a hover tooltip on the small 'Can't finish' label, so it can't be reached by keyboard and can't be read at a glance.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; help users diagnose errors [NNG-H9]; every function from the keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; hover is never the only path [desktop:HIG-POINTER]
findings.fix: When any item is Dead, use the 'failed' tone with t.down_soft and t.down_line on the header and change the pill to 'Will be dropped'. Print `why` as a second line in the row at 12px in t.down, instead of a tooltip, and list dead items first. No retry or edit control here: that would need the owner's OK.

findings.title: The page can't be used from the keyboard
findings.element: Project page › release rows, task titles, PR links, goal and checklist refs, 'Releases' back link; all sizes
findings.problem: Every control here is a div with on_click. releases.rs has no focus handle, tab stop or key handler, and kit::link adds none. A keyboard user can't expand a month row, open a task or follow a PR, and nothing can show focus. Only the app-wide actions reach this page (Cmd+K search, back and forward).
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; focus visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; arrows move within lists, one tab stop per group [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Follow the pattern backlog.rs already uses (track_focus plus on_key_down). Make the list one tab stop with a focused row drawn with a 2px t.accent ring. Up and Down move between rows, Right and Left open and close a release, Enter or Space toggles a release or opens the focused task, and Cmd+Enter follows the PR. Scroll the focused row into view with scroll_to_reveal_item.

findings.title: Plan a goal doesn't say what it does or which fixes it takes
findings.element: Review › Suggested fixes › Plan a goal, 1360x860 and 1568x1250 (review-dark-m.png, review-tall.png)
findings.problem: The button plans nothing and makes no goal: it only moves to Backlog with fixes checked. Plan waves with Claude, Create and Start all still follow. The card's pill says 3, but B4 is already In G1, so only 2 will be checked, and no row shows which ones. The only true description, "Check 2 fixes on the Backlog page", is a hover tooltip.
findings.principle: Cognitive walkthrough Q3, will users associate the action with the result [NNG-CW]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Put the count and destination on the button: "Plan 2 fixes in Backlog" (built from v.plan().len()). Make the pill count what's still open, with the rest in words, e.g. "2 open · 1 in a goal". Keep the "In G1" pill so the excluded row explains itself.

findings.title: Backlog doesn't say the checks came from the review, and has no on-screen way back
findings.element: Backlog › header and selection bar on arrival from Plan a goal (backlog-picked-dark-m.png stands in)
findings.problem: plan() sets the picks and changes page, passing no origin. The person arrives at "Plan from the backlog" with Backlog lit, "N selected" and no mention of the review, so the checks look like leftovers or something they did themselves. The way back is View › Back or ⌘←, neither shown in the window. The sidebar route, Days then Week, opens the newest review, which is the wrong one if they came from an older week.
findings.principle: User control and freedom [NNG-H3]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; walkthrough Q4, does the user see progress [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: Add one line above the list while the handed-over picks stand: "2 fixes from the Oct 29 – Nov 5 review", with a "Back to review" link that reopens that review id. Keep the origin in a new field such as m.backlog.from: Option<(i64, String)>, and clear it on Clear, Esc or when the goal is made. This is navigation only, so it fits the read-only rule. It touches the Backlog header, so agree it with that page's reviewer.

findings.title: The flow's actions can't be reached from the keyboard
findings.element: Needs you › Open review; Review › fix rows, Plan a goal, ‹ › and All weeks, Day | Week
findings.problem: taskboard-app/src has no tab_index, tab_stop or focusable call, so Tab can't land on any of these. Review has no key for Plan a goal or for opening a fix. Someone working from the keyboard can go to a page with ⌘1–6 and then has to use the pointer. Runtime behaviour wasn't driven, and gpui_kit's own code wasn't read.
findings.principle: Keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; every command reachable, Tab order and arrows in groups [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Give kit::btn, kit::seg items and clickable rows a focus handle with a tab index, a visible 2px focus ring, and Enter and Space to activate. Make Suggested fixes one tab stop with Up and Down between rows and Enter to open the issue. The same change in kit covers the rest of the app.

findings.title: The Releases flow can't be used from the keyboard
findings.element: Releases overview and project page › all rows and links, at every size (releases.rs goal_link, task_row, next_cut, release_row, overview_card)
findings.problem: Every control here is a div with on_click. None takes focus, and the app crate has no tab_index or tab_stop; track_focus exists only on the window root, text fields and a few panels. Someone on the keyboard can't expand a release, open a task or goal, follow a PR, or use the Releases back link. Only ⌘←, Esc, ⌘K and the page shortcuts work.
findings.principle: Every function works from the keyboard, with visible focus [WCAG 2.1.1] [WCAG 2.4.7]; arrows move within lists, which take one tab stop [MS-KBD]
findings.fix: Make the release list one tab stop with a roving selection. ↑/↓ moves between rows, including task rows inside open releases, Return opens the task or goal, and →/← or Space expands and collapses a release row. Draw a 2px t.accent focus ring on the current row. Give the back link and the PR links tab stops as well. Check first whether gpui_kit already offers a focus helper (not read in this review).

findings.title: Next cut rows and task rows open by different parts, and the hover misleads
findings.element: Project page › Next cut rows and goal-card task rows; Overview › card rows, in rel-webapp-dark-m.png and releases-dark-m.png
findings.problem: In Next cut only the 46px ref opens the item; clicking the title 'Link Releases from the phone app' does nothing and the row has no hover. In task rows it is the opposite: only the title text opens the task and the ref is dead, yet the whole row lights up on hover, so a click on the ref or the blank space does nothing. On overview cards, the big version block and the Unreleased strip are clickable with no hover state, only a cursor change. The Next cut ref also changes colour with state (green, blue, purple, red), so its colour doesn't say 'link'.
findings.principle: Same thing, same behaviour [NNG-H4]; a hover state must tell the truth about what's pressable, and larger targets are easier to hit [NNG-H1] [NNG-FITTS]
findings.fix: Make the whole row the target in both lists, with the PR link stopping propagation. A row click opens the task in the right panel, or the goal for G refs. Use the same t.panel_2 hover on Next cut rows, the overview's version block and the Unreleased strip. Keep the ref colour for type (task or goal) and let the mark and label carry the state.

findings.title: A cut that can't finish hides why, and doesn't say the cut will be dropped
findings.element: Project page › Next cut › a dead row and the header pill; Overview › pending pill (next_cut, wait, card). Not in the captures: code only
findings.problem: When a waited-for item can't be met, the code's own comment says the cut will be dropped, but the page shows only a red 'Can't finish'. The reason sits in a hover tooltip on a 12px label with nothing to show it has one, so keyboard users can't reach it. The header pill still reads '1 of 3 ready' in warn tone and the overview still says 'v0.14.0 pending'. This is the most important thing the Next cut section can tell the owner, and it looks like a normal wait.
findings.principle: Say what happened and what to do about it [NNG-H9]; show system status [NNG-H1]; content must not exist only on hover [WCAG 1.4.13] [WCAG 2.1.1]
findings.fix: Show w.why as a second line under the row title in t.down, 12px, wrapping rather than truncating. When any item is Dead, change the header pill to 'Can't finish' in the failed tone and the overview pill to 'v0.14.0 can't finish'. Add one plain line saying the cut will be dropped. No action in the app: cutting stays in tb.

findings.title: The task panel covers the columns the owner came to read, and the open row isn't marked
findings.element: Project page with task panel open, 1360x860 (rel-panel-dark-m.png) and 900x560 (rel-panel-dark-s.png)
findings.problem: The 480px panel floats over the page with no reflow. At 1360 it hides every Next cut state (Done, Running, 2 of 3), every PR link and date, and the counts. At 900 only 172px of page is left, so titles are cut to 'Add', 'Link' and 'Rele'. The page can't scroll sideways, so those columns can't be reached without closing the panel, although the code comment says the page stays usable. Walking the checklist task by task therefore means open, close, open. T65 also has no selected state, so nothing says which row the panel belongs to.
findings.principle: Selection is kept and shown in each pane [tablet:HIG-SPLIT] [NNG-H1]; options stay visible rather than remembered [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: While the panel is open, give the page's list a right inset of 480px so it reflows instead of being covered. At 1360 that leaves about 600px, enough for truncated titles plus the state, PR and date columns. Below that width, drop the date first, then the PR, and keep the ref and the state: about 116px of column at 900 still fits 'T68 Running'. Fill the open task's row with t.panel_2 plus a 2px t.accent left edge in task_row and next_cut, matching on the Panel::Task ref.

findings.title: Bar labels are cut mid-word while most of the axis sits empty
findings.element: Days › timeline card › lane bars at 1360 and 1728 (days-dark-m.png, days-dark-l.png)
findings.problem: Labels end as "T1 Add the WebA", "T2 Sign in with a pas", "T3 Setting" and "T3 S", with no ellipsis: text_ellipsis on the flex bar doesn't reach the bare text child. Meanwhile the axis runs 9 AM to 9 PM, so about three quarters of the width is empty and the work is squeezed into the last quarter. The hover capture shows the same at 12:01 PM with the empty part on the right. The sample's late, short day exaggerates this, but the axis isn't fitted to the work.
findings.principle: Text is not lost; primary content gets the space [WCAG 1.4.4] [SCR-1]
findings.fix: Wrap the label in an inner div with truncate so it ends in an ellipsis. Fit the axis to the day's first and last activity plus one hour each side, with a minimum span of 6 hours and always including the now line. Keep the tooltip as the full name.

findings.title: Reaching an earlier day is slow and the date control is far from the date
findings.element: Days › header › title, ‹ ›, Today, at all sizes; over 1,000px apart at 1728 (days-dark-l.png)
findings.problem: The page exists to reach any earlier day, but the only routes are one day per click or the seven tiles of the current week; three weeks back is 21 clicks, each with a reload. The stepper sits at the far right while the date it changes is at the far left. The title "Today" also never states the date, so the reader has to find the selected tile.
findings.principle: Flexibility and efficiency of use [NNG-H7]; related controls grouped and close together [NNG-FITTS]
findings.fix: Move ‹ › directly before the title, so a longer title doesn't move them. Make the title open a month calendar pop-up limited to oldest through today, with past weeks reachable from it. Show "Today · Fri, Nov 6" in the title. This is navigation only, so it stays within the read-only rule.

findings.title: Changing the date removes the whole page, and an error strands it
findings.element: Days › page shell during a date change and on a failed load
findings.problem: set_date clears m.data.days, so render returns only "Loading…" or the error text: header, stepper, tiles and chart all disappear until the answer lands. Repeated ‹ clicks fall on nothing, the page blinks on each step, and if the load fails there is no retry and no way to return to today on the page; only Cmd-R or leaving and returning remain. Read from code, not observed.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status; no dead ends [NNG-H1] [NNG-H3] [NNG-H9]
findings.fix: Keep the previous view on screen until the new answer lands, updating the title and tile selection at once and dimming the content to about 60%. Always render the header. On an error, show it inline under the header with a Retry button and leave ‹ › and Today working.

findings.title: Week bars can't be read per project
findings.element: Days › week card › stacked columns and tooltip (hover-days-bar-dark-m.png)
findings.problem: The chart is stacked by project, but the tooltip gives only the total: "Wednesday, November 4: 7h 18m agent time, 4 done". Project share can only be estimated by eye, and only by colour. From the fifth project on, every project is the same grey, so their segments merge and can't be told apart, which matters for an owner running many agents. The sample has two projects, so this wasn't seen on screen.
findings.principle: Colour isn't the only signal [WCAG 1.4.1]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Add each project to the tooltip on separate lines, for example "api 2h 55m" and "webapp 4h 23m", in stack order. Past four projects, add palette slots checked for separation, or fold the smallest into one "Other" segment that the tooltip itemises.

findings.title: Project toggles grow with the board and repeat as a legend
findings.element: Days › header › project toggles; week card › legend
findings.problem: There is one 30px chip per project in a wrapping row with no limit. Two fit at 900 wide (days-dark-s.png), but more will wrap and push the date controls onto a new line, moving them between boards. The week card then repeats the same names and colours as a legend directly below. The sample has two projects, so the wrap wasn't seen.
findings.principle: Owner lesson L2: a set that grows uses a pop-up menu; one fact, one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Show chips up to four projects. Past that, use one pop-up menu button labelled "Projects · 3 of 7" with checkable colour-swatched rows. Keep the week card's legend only in the pop-up case, and remove it while the chips are visible, since they already act as the key.

findings.title: A hidden project's toggle fails text contrast
findings.element: Days › header › project toggle, off state, both themes
findings.problem: An off chip uses t.faint on the page background: about 2.8:1 in light (#8a95a3 on #f6f7f9) and about 4.3:1 in dark (#6f7a88 on #0f1216), at 12.5px. The chip is still a working control, which is how the project is brought back, so the disabled exemption doesn't apply. Ratios were computed by hand from theme.rs; this state isn't in the captures.
findings.principle: Text contrast at least 4.5:1 [WCAG 1.4.3]
findings.fix: Use t.muted for off chips: #5f6b7a in light and #a1abb8 in dark, both above 4.5:1 on the page background. The outlined swatch and missing fill still mark the off state.

findings.title: The last visible project's toggle silently does nothing
findings.element: Days › header › project toggle when only one project is shown
findings.problem: toggle() returns without change when a click would hide the last project, but the chip keeps its pointer cursor and its "Hide webapp" tooltip. The click looks broken.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status; constraints shown before the error [NNG-H1] [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: When one project is left, change its tooltip to "At least one project stays shown", use the default cursor and skip the click handler.

findings.title: At the smallest window the day's timeline falls below the fold
findings.element: Days › KPI tiles, week card, rail at 900x560 (days-dark-s.png)
findings.problem: Tile labels wrap, "5h 36m" breaks over two lines, and values no longer share a baseline. The tile row grows to about 135px, so the header, tiles and the fixed 170px chart fill the window, and the timeline isn't visible at all. By code, the rail also wraps under all four left cards below about 1,040 wide, as a 300px column beside empty space. Even at larger sizes the week chart is the loudest thing on a page about one day.
findings.principle: The work dominates; narrowing keeps the order [SCR-1] [SCR-2] [SCR-6]
findings.fix: Set whitespace_nowrap on tile values and shorten labels to one line, for example "Human est." and "Waiting". Under 1,040 wide, lay the tiles out 3 by 2 or drop the tile padding to 8px. Under 700 tall, reduce the chart's H to 100. Consider moving the timeline above the week card, and when the rail wraps lay its cards in two columns across the full width.

findings.title: Clustered marks can't be read
findings.element: Days › timeline card › marks row, 1360 (days-dark-m.png) and 1728
findings.problem: Marks are 8px dots with 12x12 hover targets that overlap when events are close, as in the Question and Commit pair near 8 PM and the Commit run near 7 PM. Only the topmost target gets a tooltip, so the others can't be read. The tooltip is also the only route to a mark's text.
findings.principle: Targets at least 24 x 24 CSS px or spaced apart [WCAG 2.5.8]; no hover-only path [NNG-FITTS]
findings.fix: Merge marks within 12px into one 24px-tall hover target whose tooltip lists each mark in time order, with its 12-hour time, ref and text. Make the row's target 24px tall even for single marks.

findings.title: The timeline has no heading and the date scrolls away
findings.element: Days › timeline card, all sizes
findings.problem: Every neighbouring card has a title, but this one opens with its legend. The page header scrolls with the content, so once the reader is on the timeline nothing says which day it shows. That matters because the card above it covers a week, and a past day looks identical to today apart from the now line.
findings.principle: Headings describe their content [WCAG 2.4.6]; every group labelled the same way [SEC-6]
findings.fix: Add an h2 carrying the fact itself, "Fri, Nov 6", which is not a filler label, with the legend at the right of that row like the other cards. Alternatively make the header sticky inside the scroller.

findings.title: Usage, host and slot rows squeeze their readings into a 104px label column
findings.element: Days › timeline card › Usage, host and slot rows
findings.problem: Lines such as "full 2 times · 45m", "1 task waited 30m", every "T12 idle 2h" and "Hourly budget used up" sit in a 104px column with no truncation, so they probably wrap. The idle list has no limit, so the label column can grow while the band stays 22px tall. The Usage chart has dashed lines at 50% and 100% with no scale labels, so a value can't be read without hovering. None of these rows appear in the sample, so this comes from code only.
findings.principle: Text is not lost, and recognition rather than recall [WCAG 1.4.4] [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Show the slot and host detail as one line under the band, spanning the full card width, and cap idle tasks at three with "+2 more" in a tooltip. Label the Usage gridlines 50% and 100% at the left of the plot, and add the project swatch to slot rows to match the lanes.

findings.title: Below about 1040 wide the rail drops under everything at half width
findings.element: Days › lower layout at window widths under about 1040: days-s.png, 900 wide
findings.problem: The left column (min 420) plus the rail (fixed 300) plus gap needs 736 px, so at 900 wide the flex-wrap sends the rail below Done today. It keeps w(px(300.)), leaving about 297 px beside it empty, and six cards stack in one thin column. The page roughly doubles in length, and Notable, the day's summary, ends up last.
findings.principle: The order holds as it narrows [SCR-6]; desktop window range [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: When the rail wraps (viewport under 1040), make it .w_full().flex().flex_row().flex_wrap() and give each card .flex_1().min_w(px(280.)), so the cards fill two columns of about 290 px. Pair the cards by scope from R6: Notable with Waiting on you, Hours saved with Tasks done.

findings.title: The lower cards have no maximum width
findings.element: Days › How long tasks took and Done today on a large display, code path; widest capture is about 1363 wide
findings.problem: The page column is w_full() and left is flex_1 with no max width, so on a wide display bars keep stretching and each Done today time sits further from its title. It is already about 650 px away in days-900.png, with only the hover fill to connect the two. The rail stays 300 while the left grows.
findings.principle: Nothing stretches past a readable line length at the maximum window size [HIG-MACOS] [tablet:AND-T2]
findings.fix: Add .max_w(px(1600.)) to the page's inner column. In Done rows, move the time next to the title's end or add a divider line per row if the column stays wider than about 900.

findings.title: Failed and lost tasks look like any other row
findings.element: Days › How long tasks took › state column, failed or lost task (code; not in the sample captures)
findings.problem: state_c gives warn_fg to "needs you" and muted grey to everything else, so "failed" and "lost" are the same quiet 12px text as "so far", on a bar in normal project colour. Those are the rows the owner most needs in "how the work went". The timeline already uses t.down and down_soft for them.
findings.principle: Consistency [NNG-H4]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Set state_c to t.down for "failed" and "lost" (6.57:1 light, 5.80:1 dark on card) with FontWeight::SEMIBOLD, matching bar_colors.

findings.title: The task list is silently cut to 8 and its median line carries no information
findings.element: Days › How long tasks took: days-tall.png, days-900.png
findings.problem: View::of uses .take(8), so the card shows 8 tasks in a week with 15 done, with no count and no way to see the rest; the title suggests it covers the week's tasks. The median is computed over the whole week, so all 8 long tasks pass it and the same tick crosses every bar, forming a heavy vertical rule that says nothing about any row. In dark mode the tick is also 2.52:1 on webapp and 2.99:1 on api.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; every element earns its place [SCR-5]
findings.fix: Title it "Longest tasks · Nov 1 – Nov 7" with a muted "8 of 23", and add the same Show all link Done today has. Drop the per-row tick and keep "median 1h 36m" as text in the legend, or draw it once as a single line behind the bars at t.border_2.

findings.title: A row's project is shown by colour alone
findings.element: Days › How long tasks took bars, Done today swatches; light and dark
findings.problem: Neither list prints the project name, which sits only in the tooltip. Past four projects project_color falls back to one grey, so an owner with many projects can't tell them apart, and that is this owner's normal use. In light mode the webapp swatch is 2.17:1 on white, so the small swatch is faint too.
findings.principle: Use of colour [WCAG 1.4.1]; non-text contrast [WCAG 1.4.11]
findings.fix: Add a muted 12px project name in Done rows between the title and the time, and in task rows after the title once more than one project is shown. Darken the light webapp slot from #eda100 to at least 3:1 on white, around #b87a00, then re-check colour-blind separation.

findings.title: Notable names tasks by bare ref and they can't be opened
findings.element: Days › Notable › "longest wait on you · T3", "longest task · T2": days-tall.png, days-s.png
findings.problem: Elsewhere on the page a task ref opens the right panel. In Notable it is plain text with no title, so the owner has to remember what T3 is or hunt for it further down. "3 at once" and "busiest hour · 4 events" are also vague about what ran and what counts as an event.
findings.principle: Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; tasks open in the right panel (owner's one-home rule)
findings.fix: Carry the ref in notes as Option<String>, and make the note a row with the same hover and on_click open_task as task rows. Show the title with truncate: "longest wait on you · T3 Settings passkey". Reword to "3 agents at once" and "4 commits, PRs and questions".

findings.title: The Waiting on you strip is unlabelled and hides waits
findings.element: Days › Waiting on you › strip: days-tall.png, days-s.png
findings.problem: Nothing says the tall tick is "usual" or that a square is one wait, and the median in the subtitle isn't plotted. Each square is 10 px with a 2 px card-colour border, so about 6 px is visible, and that is the only hover target for which task waited (under the 24 px floor). Every wait of 60m or more is clamped to x=1.0, so the worst waits stack on one spot and only the top tooltip can be reached. Squares aren't clickable. With no waits the card still shows 0m and an empty scale.
findings.principle: Target size [WCAG 2.5.8]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Label the tick with a small "usual 18m" above it, and remove usual from the subtitle. Replace the squares with a list of up to 3 waits ("36m · T3 Settings passkey") opening the task, with the strip above as a summary; the rows are then the 24 px-plus targets. With no waits, show only "No waits" in muted text and drop the strip.

findings.title: Tasks done card: quiet selected day, weak last-week line, muddled subtitle
findings.element: Days › Tasks done this week: days-tall.png, days-900.png
findings.problem: The selected day is only a band at 1.17:1 against the card in dark and 1.16:1 in light, and its label stays plain, while Hours saved bolds "Fr". Where the last-week line crosses a bar it is 2.14:1 in dark. Bars use the accent blue, close to the api project blue beside them (#3563e9 and #2a78d6 light), so they can read as api's work. The subtitle "last week 16 · 6 PRs, last week 8" repeats "last week" and adds PRs to a tasks card; with merged counts it grows long enough that it will likely wrap in the 272 px of card width.
findings.principle: Non-text contrast [WCAG 1.4.11]; use of colour [WCAG 1.4.1]; one look per role [SEC-4]
findings.fix: Bold the selected label in t.text, as in Hours saved. Give the last-week line a 1px card-colour halo. Use a neutral bar colour (t.text_2 at reduced strength) so blue stays api. Split the subtitle into two muted lines: "16 last week" and "6 PRs (8) · 4 merged (4)".

findings.title: Hours saved can't be read per day or squared with the agent chart
findings.element: Days › Hours saved this week: days-tall.png, days-s.png
findings.problem: The chart has no hover values, unlike the Usage row and Tasks done, so a day's figure can only be estimated between 0, 40h and 80h. The breakdown says "24h agent" while the week chart above adds up to roughly 28h (read from the bars), because this uses est_agent_min and the label doesn't say so. The legend draws last week as a solid line, but the chart draws it dashed. "−16h on last week" doesn't say it compares the same point in the week.
findings.principle: Consistency [NNG-H4]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Overlay seven flex_1 hover targets, as usage_row does, with a tip such as "Thu · 52h · week before 58h". Relabel to "79h human estimate − 24h agent on estimated tasks". Draw the legend's last-week swatch dashed. Change the delta to "16h behind last week at this point".

findings.title: Planning shows better or worse by colour only, and "was" has no period
findings.element: Days › Planning, last 30 days (code; card not present in any capture, which may be the sample's)
findings.problem: Green or red on the value is the only better-or-worse signal, and lower being better isn't stated anywhere, so "1.2 was 0.9" can't be judged without colour. "was" doesn't say it means the half year before. "Fix rounds a task" and "Questions a task" read as fragments.
findings.principle: Use of colour [WCAG 1.4.1]; match with the real world [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Add ↓ or ↑ before the value with better or worse in the tooltip. Add a muted line under the title: "Lower is better · was: the 6 months before". Reword to "Fix rounds per task" and "Questions per task", and check the longest label still fits the 300 px rail.

findings.title: Show all renders the whole Done list without virtualizing
findings.element: Days › Done today › Show all N
findings.problem: Expanding renders every finished row as plain .children(rows) inside the page scroller. A busy day with many agents is a long list, and this breaks the owner's rule that long lists are virtualized. The page also gets longer in one step.
findings.principle: Owner rule: long lists virtualized; flexibility and efficiency [NNG-H7]
findings.fix: Reveal in steps of 50 ("Show 50 more", then "Show fewer") so the page keeps one scroller, or move the expanded list to a gpui list sized to the page scroller. Avoid a fixed-height inner scroller, which nests same-direction scrolling [HIG-SCROLL].

findings.title: Task titles truncate at any window width and start on ragged edges
findings.element: Days › How long tasks took › name column: days-900.png, days-s.png
findings.problem: The name column is fixed at 230 px, so "Add the WebAuthn registration en…" and "Retry webhook deliveries with bac…" are cut at every size while the bars take all extra width; the full title is only in a hover tooltip. Refs have no fixed width, so titles start at different x positions (T19 against T2), unlike Done today's aligned 52 px ref column.
findings.principle: Aligned to a grid [SCR-4]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Give the ref a fixed width of 40 px, matching across both cards. Make the name column .w(relative(0.4)).min_w(px(230.)).max_w(px(420.)) so titles get space before bars do.

findings.title: Changing week blanks the page, and a failed load leaves no week controls
findings.element: Weekly review › header › ‹, All weeks, › and Week, during load or error
findings.problem: pick() clears the review, so each step renders an empty title, 'Loading…' and only Day/Week. ‹ and › vanish under the pointer, so stepping back several weeks can miss, and the scroll position is lost with the content. If the load fails, the error shows with no week controls and no retry. Clicking Week on this page does nothing, so the way out is Day then Week, or Cmd+R. Latency wasn't measured, so how long the blank lasts is unknown.
findings.principle: User control and freedom [NNG-H3]; error recovery [NNG-H9]; system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Keep the previous review on screen, dimmed to 60%, until the new one lands. Always render the nav from the list, with the title from the list entry's period. On failure, keep the nav and show the error with a Try again button that calls refresh. Make Week on the Review page return to the newest review when an older one is open.

findings.title: Narrow windows orphan a KPI and strand the rail
findings.element: Weekly review › KPIs and rail at 900x560 (review-dark-s.png), and at windows below about 1080 wide
findings.problem: Four cards at min width 170 need 716px but about 597px is available, so 'Failed, then rerun' takes a full-width row for one digit. That card pushes Suggested fixes down, and only two fix rows fit the fold at the minimum window. From code, the 340px rail also wraps below the left column and stays 340 wide, leaving about 257px empty beside it. An open right panel probably triggers both at larger windows.
findings.principle: Narrowing keeps the order [SCR-6]; the work dominates [SCR-1]
findings.fix: Set the KPI min width to 130 so four fit at 597px (4 x 130 + 36 = 556), or use a fixed 2x2 grid below that width. Drop the delta row's reserved height when the row wraps. When the rail wraps, set it to w_full, or lay its two cards side by side.

findings.title: Category colours change meaning between weeks
findings.element: Weekly review › Where the time went (review-dark-m.png against review-older-dark-m.png)
findings.problem: category_color uses rank in the week, not the category. Load wait is teal in Oct 22 – Oct 29 and grey in Oct 29 – Nov 5, where Git takes teal. Stepping with ‹ › to compare weeks, the owner tracks a colour that now means something else. Every category past the fifth is the same grey, so those segments can't be told apart.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Map colour by category name (build, test, edit, read, git, load wait and so on) from a fixed table, shared with any other page that shows categories. Use grey only for unknown names, and merge the tail into one 'Other' row past six.

findings.title: Plan a goal overwrites Backlog picks and its label hides what it does
findings.element: Weekly review › Suggested fixes › Plan a goal
findings.problem: plan() assigns m.backlog.picked = refs and resets the project and kind filters, so any issues already checked on the Backlog are silently dropped. The button only goes to the Backlog with fixes checked, which only the hover tooltip says. The pill says 3 while the button acts on 2, because B4 is already in G1, and nothing visible explains the gap.
findings.principle: Unsaved work survives in-app actions [NNG-H3] [NNG-H5]; walkthrough question 3 [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: Merge the refs into the existing picks without duplicates. Label the button with its effect and count, for example 'Plan 2 fixes'. Count only open, untriaged fixes in the pill, or show '2 of 3 open'.

findings.title: Timeouts KPI and Timed out tab show different numbers
findings.element: Weekly review › KPIs › Timeouts and Commands › Timed out (review-dark-m.png, review-800.png)
findings.problem: The KPI says 2 and the tab says 'Timed out 1', because one counts events and the other counts distinct commands. Neither says so, and the two sit a full screen apart, so they read as a contradiction. Rerun happens to match, which makes the mismatch more surprising.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Make the tab count the same unit as the KPI by summing each command's count, so it reads 'Timed out 2'. The row's '2 timeouts' detail then explains it.

findings.title: A failed filing leaves suggestions with no next step
findings.element: Weekly review › Suggested fixes, filing failed (code only)
findings.problem: The failure shows in the same muted 13px text as a normal note, so it is easy to miss. With nothing filed there are no fix rows and no Plan a goal, so the suggestions can only be read. The card that should be acted on becomes a dead end, with no retry or next step. 'Filing these…' while running also has no indicator beyond its text.
findings.principle: Help users recover from errors [NNG-H9]; system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Show the failure in t.warn with a warning mark, and say what to do next in words. Add a one-click 'File again' signal. That is a new write action, so it needs the owner's OK. Without it, name the `tb` command that retries.

findings.title: 'Weekly reviews are off' gives no way forward
findings.element: Weekly review › first review callout, reviews off (code only)
findings.problem: The state says reviews are off but not why, or where to turn them on. A search of the app's source found no Weekly review setting outside Home, so the owner has nowhere obvious to go. In the same function, a load error is shown only when no time is tracked, so with tracked time the error is hidden.
findings.principle: Empty states have a way forward [mobile:NNG-EMPTY]; help in context [NNG-H10]; system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Add one muted line naming the exact setting or `tb` command that enables reviews. An in-app toggle would be a new write, so it needs the owner's OK. Show errs.review whether or not time is tracked.

findings.title: Future days in the first-review strip fail text contrast
findings.element: Weekly review › first review callout › day strip, future days (code only), both themes
findings.problem: Future days use t.faint on t.card at 10.5px and 14px. That is about 3.0:1 in light (#8a95a3 on #ffffff) and 3.8:1 in dark (#6f7a88 on #1a1f26), so the dates leading up to the review are hard to read. Ratios were worked out by hand from the theme values.
findings.principle: Contrast minimum 4.5:1 [WCAG 1.4.3]
findings.fix: Use t.muted for future days (#5f6b7a in light, #a1abb8 in dark), and keep the past/future difference through the fill and border already in place.

findings.title: Selected segment is nearly invisible in dark mode
findings.element: Weekly review › header › Day/Week and Commands tabs, dark (review-dark-m.png, review-800.png)
findings.problem: The selected item's fill (#1a1f26) on the track (#232931) is about 1.13:1, and weight stays medium, so selection rests almost entirely on a text colour change. The tab that decides what the Commands list shows is easy to misread. Light mode is clearer because white and a shadow do the work.
findings.principle: Non-text contrast and use of colour [WCAG 1.4.11] [WCAG 1.4.1]
findings.fix: In kit::seg, make the selected label semibold and add a 1px t.border_2 border to the selected item. Check that the border reaches 3:1 against the track in dark, and raise it if not.

findings.title: Command row details are misleading or repeated
findings.element: Weekly review › Commands › Slow repeated and Rerun rows (review-800.png; Rerun from code)
findings.problem: 'median · p90 12 min · 14 runs   7 min' puts the word median beside the p90 value while its own value sits at the far right, so it reads as a label with no number. Rerun rows show the task ref twice, once as the mono ref and again in the detail ('T12 · 3 runs, then passed').
findings.principle: Match the real world [NNG-H2]; one fact, one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Change the detail to '14 runs · p90 12 min' and the right-hand value to 'median 7 min', or add a small column label. Remove the task ref from the rerun detail so it reads '3 runs, then passed', and update the test that asserts the old string.

findings.title: Row bars use a different scale from the stacked bar
findings.element: Weekly review › Waiting on you, By project, Slowest tasks (review-tall.png)
findings.problem: shares() scales each bar to the longest row, so Question and webapp show full bars at 67% and 71% of their totals. Just beside them, Where the time went shows true share of the total. A full bar reads as 100%, so the size of the top item is overstated.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; clear hierarchy [NNG-VH]
findings.fix: For Waiting on you and By project, divide by the section total instead of the max. Keep longest-row scaling only for Slowest tasks and Commands, whose rows aren't parts of one total.

findings.title: Header claims "0 unreleased tasks" before anything has loaded
findings.element: Releases › page header summary › Loading and Can't load states, from code (line 823)
findings.problem: With no state yet, projects is empty, so `lists.iter().all(Option::is_some)` is true and the summary renders "0 unreleased tasks" beside "Loading…" or "Can't load the board.". The page reports a clean count it does not have.
findings.principle: Commands and status never report what they didn't have [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Add `!projects.is_empty() &&` to the condition, so the summary appears only once every listed project has answered.

findings.title: Cards do not say what shipped
findings.element: Releases › project card › latest release block, all sizes
findings.problem: The primary task includes checking what is in each release, but the card gives only the version, time and task count. Row.headline, the first line of the notes, is computed and never shown on the overview. The owner has to open each project to learn what a release was about. The sample may have no notes, but the code never shows them either way.
findings.principle: Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; frequent in view [SEC-8]
findings.fix: Add the headline under the version at 13px text_2, one truncated line, and render it only when notes exist so no blank line or filler appears.

findings.title: Failed row cuts the time and loses PM
findings.element: Releases › project card › previous release row at 1360x860 ("Oct 21, 8:38…" in releases-dark-m.png, releases-light-m.png)
findings.problem: At a 341px card, the Failed pill squeezes the flexible time column, so the time truncates and loses AM/PM. At 344px (releases-dark-l.png) it just fits, so 3px decides it. Rows from a previous year ("Oct 21, 2025, 8:38 PM") are longer and will probably cut even without a pill.
findings.principle: Owner rule: 12-hour times with AM/PM; sections align and hold at each width [SCR-4]
findings.fix: Stop the time from shrinking (flex_none, whitespace_nowrap), and put the Failed pill in the count's slot, since a failed release's work has gone back to Unreleased and "0 tasks" adds little. Also raise CARD_MIN from 340 to 380 so a prior-year date fits beside the count.

findings.title: Grid reserves columns for projects that don't exist
findings.element: Releases › card grid at 1360x860 and 1728x1084 (releases-dark-m.png, releases-dark-l.png)
findings.problem: columns() counts what fits, not how many projects there are, so two projects get a 3-column grid at 1360 and a 4-column grid at 1728, padded with empty spacers. At 1728 about half the main area is empty, while the cards stay about 344px wide and tight enough to nearly cut text. The two-project count is the sample's, but any board with fewer projects than columns does this. The task panel floats over the right edge, which may explain some of the free room, but its 480px does not account for the empty columns.
findings.principle: The work dominates [SCR-1]; large displays used to show more [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: Use cols = min(fit, projects.len()), remove the spacers when there is only one row, and cap cards at max_w 560. That gives two 520px cards at 1360 and two 560px cards at 1728.

findings.title: Latest block and Unreleased tile give no sign they are clickable
findings.element: Releases › project card › latest release block and Unreleased tile, pointer hover
findings.problem: Both have a pointer cursor but no hover state, while the previous rows just below do highlight (lines 788-791 against 747-775). The Unreleased tile reads as a status strip, so the owner may not find the route to what the next cut waits for, and the same card treats clickable items in two ways.
findings.principle: States are designed [NNG-H1]; one look per role [SEC-4]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Give both the same hover as the rows: panel_2 on the latest block, and one step brighter on the tile. Add a trailing "›" in muted to the tile.

findings.title: "Unreleased 0 tasks" takes a full tile and leads nowhere useful
findings.element: Releases › api card › Unreleased tile (releases-dark-m.png, releases-light-m.png, releases-dark-s.png)
findings.problem: With nothing waiting, the tile still takes about 44px at the same size as a live one and carries no news, which works against the owner's no-filler rule. Clicking it opens the project page, where top() leaves out the Unreleased section altogether, so the click does not lead to anything about Unreleased. At 900x560 it also helps push webapp's rows below the fold.
findings.principle: Everything earns its place [SCR-5]; aesthetic and minimalist design [NNG-H8]; owner rule: no filler labels
findings.fix: Render the tile only when unreleased > 0 or a cut is pending. The header summary already gives the total across projects.

findings.title: "N releases" link is under the 24px target floor
findings.element: Releases › project card › header › "1 release" / "9 releases" link, all sizes
findings.problem: The link's height is its 13px text at 1.4 line height, about 18px. The head has no bottom padding, so it sits directly against the latest block's click area and fails the spacing exception. A slightly low click opens the release in place of the list. Figures are read from code, not measured.
findings.principle: Target size minimum [WCAG 2.5.8]; adjacent targets spaced [NNG-FITTS]
findings.fix: Give the link h 24 with items_center, and add 4px of padding under the head so the two targets don't touch.

findings.title: A project with no releases gets no empty state
findings.element: Releases › project card › no releases state, from code (lines 745-758)
findings.problem: A project that has releases turned on but no cuts shows a blue "0 releases" link and a grey "Unreleased 0 tasks" tile, with no version line and no message. It looks broken or half loaded. The project page does say "No releases yet", but the overview doesn't.
findings.principle: Empty states are designed [mobile:NNG-EMPTY]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: When latest is None, show kit::help("No releases yet") where the version sits, and replace the "0 releases" link with plain muted text or remove it.

findings.title: Unreleased and the newest release are unbounded and not virtualized
findings.element: Project page › Item::Top and open release rows (rel-webapp-dark-s.png at 900x560, rel-api-dark-m.png at 1360x860, rel-tall.png)
findings.problem: Item::Top renders the header, every Unreleased task and every task in the newest release as one list item, and an open older release is also one item. That breaks the owner's rule that long lists are virtualized: only the month rows are. Neither section can be collapsed. At 900x560 Unreleased alone fills the view and v0.13.0 starts below the fold. With sample data, October starts about 1000px down in rel-tall.png, and a 19-task release pushes it further in rel-api-dark-m.png. A busy board will be worse, and 'what shipped' is half of the task.
findings.principle: Owner rule: long lists virtualized. Frequent in view, rare behind [SEC-8]; large displays show more in fewer levels [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: Split Top into list items: header, Unreleased head, Next cut, one item per goal group, and the same for the newest and any open release, so the list virtualizes them. Show the first 8 tasks of a long group with 'Show all 19 tasks' opening in place. Optional: at content widths of 1400 and up, use the roughly 530px left empty at 1728 for Next cut in a right column, if the task panel leaves room.

findings.title: A failed release explains nothing when opened
findings.element: Project page › v0.11.1 row, open (capture-failed-open-dark-l.png, rel-low.png); the newest-release section when it has failed
findings.problem: The chevron promises detail, but the row opens to its headline repeated and then 'No tasks' (work() when groups are empty; the text is cut off at the bottom of the capture). It doesn't say when it failed, or that its work went back to Unreleased, which the code knows from failed_at and its comment. '0 tasks' reads as if it never held anything. If the newest release fails, the section shows 'Failed' and nothing marks the release that is actually current. The 'Failed 1' stat also gives no way to reach the row.
findings.principle: Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors [NNG-H9]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: For a failed release, show 'Failed Oct 21, 9:12 PM · its work went back to Unreleased' in place of 'No tasks', and hide the repeated headline. Listing the tasks it held needs a board API change, so that part needs the owner's OK. Keep the 'Latest' pill on the newest release that hasn't failed. Make the Failed stat scroll to the newest failed row when it is above 0, using scroll_to_reveal_item.

findings.title: A failed fetch shows 'Loading…' forever
findings.element: Project page › work() and project_page(); app.rs lines 1462-1471; not captured
findings.problem: `if let Ok(v)` drops every error from GET /releases and GET /releases/:id. If an open row or the Unreleased detail fails while the board is up, the page keeps saying 'Loading…' with no error or way forward. The owner can't tell a slow answer from a broken one.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; plain-language errors with a way forward [NNG-H9]; each area has an error state [tablet:AND-CANON]
findings.fix: Record errors by key, as data.errs does for tasks, and show 'Couldn't load v0.11.0.' with a Retry link in place of 'Loading…'. Retry only fetches again, so it stays within the read-only rule. Clear the error on the next good answer.

findings.title: Opening a row near the window's bottom shows nothing
findings.element: Project page › v0.11.0 row at 1728x1084 (rel-open-dark-l.png); v0.11.1 (capture-failed-open-dark-l.png)
findings.problem: In rel-open-dark-l.png the row is open but none of its content is in view: the only change is the chevron. v0.11.1 shows one line and a cut-off second. The click handler doesn't scroll, so the owner has to scroll to see whether anything happened. It will happen more at short windows, where more rows sit near the bottom edge.
findings.principle: After the action, users see progress [NNG-CW]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: After a row opens and its detail lands, call scroll_to_reveal_item for that row, as the linked-release path in project_page already does, so the row and its first lines are in view. Don't scroll on close.

findings.title: Task rows highlight as a whole but only part of them clicks, and the two lists disagree
findings.element: Project page › task_row and next_cut rows (T64 hovered in rel-webapp-dark-m.png; T15 in rel-api-dark-m.png)
findings.problem: A task row highlights across its full width, but only the title text opens the task, so a click on the empty middle does nothing. The title also doesn't look like a link until hovered. In the Next cut the rule flips: the coloured ref opens the task and the title does nothing. The same object behaves two ways a few pixels apart, and the owner uses these all day.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; frequent targets are large [NNG-FITTS]; looks like what it is [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Make the whole row the target in both lists, opening the task in the right panel or the goal on its page. Keep the PR link as its own target and stop its click from reaching the row. Apply the same hover to checklist rows.

findings.title: Filler labels and facts repeated next to each other
findings.element: Project page › newest release and open rows (rel-api-dark-m.png, rel-failed-dark-l.png, rel-webapp-dark-m.png)
findings.problem: Against the owner's no-filler rule: 'No goal' heads the only group in v2.3.0 and says nothing. '19 tasks' sits twice within 60px, in the meta line and the group header, and a one-group release always repeats its count. An open row repeats its headline as the first line of notes ('Search, keyboard shortcuts' twice in rel-failed-dark-l.png). The breadcrumb's 'webapp' sits right above the 'webapp' title.
findings.principle: Owner rule: no filler labels. One fact, one place [SEC-7]; aesthetic and minimalist design [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: In work(), skip the head row when the only group has no goal. Drop the group count when a release has a single group. In release_row, show notes without their first line, since the row already shows it. Drop the current-page crumb and show only the 'Releases' back link above the title.

findings.title: Plan a goal silently replaces what was already checked
findings.element: Review › Plan a goal → Backlog selection and project filter
findings.problem: plan() assigns m.backlog.picked = refs, so any issues the person had checked on Backlog are gone without a word. It also resets the project filter to all with no notice. Someone halfway through picking a goal who looks at the review loses that work, with no undo.
findings.principle: Unsaved input survives in-app actions [NNG-H3] [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Add the fixes to the existing picks instead of replacing them, skipping any already there. Say so in the R18 line: "2 fixes from the Oct 29 – Nov 5 review added to 4 checked".

findings.title: Fixes not yet loaded drop out of the selection with no notice
findings.element: Backlog › selection count and New backlog goal, on a backlog over 100 issues, or with a fix triaged after the review loaded
findings.problem: selected() and draft() count only picks among rows already held, and the first fetch holds 100 (PAGE). A fix further down isn't counted until the list is scrolled that far. The tooltip says 3, Backlog says 2 selected, and the goal can be planned without the third. Fixes from older weeks are the likeliest to be affected. How often depends on real backlog size and the board's sort order, which I didn't trace.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; error prevention [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: On handover, fetch the picked issues by id (Paged::fetch already has an ids path) and add them to held before counting. If one is no longer open, say so in the R18 line: "1 of 3 fixes is no longer open".

findings.title: The bar's key hints fail on arrival, then one key can drop every handed-over fix
findings.element: Backlog › selection bar on arrival: Move to goal M, Set priority P, Defer D, Drop X (backlog-picked-dark-m.png)
findings.problem: The page takes focus only on a mouse press, and I found no other code that focuses it, so M, P, D and X should do nothing on arrival even though they're shown. After any click they go live, and X or D acts at once on a selection the app made, not the person. bulk() has no confirm, and its toast has no Undo. The Backlog reviewer owns Drop itself; the handover is what widens its reach.
findings.principle: Error prevention [NNG-H5]; user control and freedom [NNG-H3]; destructive actions can be undone or confirmed [NNG-H3]
findings.fix: Focus plan-page when arriving from Plan a goal so the hints are true. Add an Undo to the "Dropped 2 issues" and "Deferred 2 issues" toasts for about 8 seconds. If Undo isn't possible, confirm with "Drop 2 issues?" when the picks came from a review.

findings.title: The page Open review lands on never says it's the review
findings.element: Review › header and sidebar, 1360x860 (review-dark-m.png)
findings.problem: The person presses Open review and lands on a page titled "Oct 29 – Nov 5" with Days lit in the sidebar. The word review appears nowhere on the page; Week in the Day | Week toggle is the only clue. It reads like a Days view, which also makes the page hard to find again.
findings.principle: Headings describe their content [WCAG 2.4.6]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; match with the real world [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Title it "Weekly review · Oct 29 – Nov 5", keeping "vs Oct 22 – Oct 29" beside it. Leaving the page under Days is fine once the heading names it.

findings.title: Opening the review clears the to-do while its fixes are still undone
findings.element: Needs you › Your to-dos › Weekly review row; Review › mark_seen
findings.problem: mark_seen fires as soon as the review draws, including when it's reached from the Week toggle, so the item goes with no feedback. If the person is interrupted before Plan a goal, nothing on Needs you points back to the fixes. Only the bare Backlog count remains. The reminder ends at reading, not at acting, which is the task this flow exists for.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Needs the owner's OK, because the board's rule today is that a review stays until opened. Keep the row until no fix is untriaged, reworded after opening to "2 fixes from the Oct 29 – Nov 5 review not planned". Its existing Later menu covers putting it off. If the rule stays, show the same line as a quiet note on the Backlog sidebar row.

findings.title: When filing fixes fails, the page is a dead end
findings.element: Review › Suggested fixes, fixes state failed (from code, not captured)
